title: src/db/provisioning.zig: session-scoped advisory lock can be left held by an idle pooled connection, hanging all subsequent tenant provisioning under full-suite zig build test
registered_by: TEST-RUNNER (WF03-GH528-20260807 Step 4, incidental finding during verification of an unrelated fix)
related_to: ISS-0131 (OPEN — C40P01 deadlock between provisionTenantSchema and concurrent migrations, different failure mode)
ISS-0209 (RESOLVED — DROP SCHEMA CASCADE race in test_api08_auth.zig, different failure mode)
scope: src/db/provisioning.zig acquireAdvisoryLock/releaseAdvisoryLock — affects any full-suite zig build test run that provisions tenant schemas concurrently.
symptom: A full `zig build test` run hangs indefinitely (25+ minutes observed, no progress) with no error output. pg_stat_activity on the test database shows one backend holding a session-scoped PostgreSQL advisory lock (acquired via `SELECT pg_advisory_lock(hashtext($1 || $2)::bigint)`) while sitting `idle` (not executing any query), and one or more other backends permanently blocked waiting on `SELECT pg_advisory_lock(...)` for the same key. Reproduced twice independently in one session (different backend PIDs each time), both times within a full-suite run; never reproduced when running a scoped subset (e.g. `zig build test-bpm-src`) in isolation or even two-at-a-time concurrently.
root_cause_analysis: provisionTenantSchema() (src/db/provisioning.zig:94-125) acquires a session-scoped advisory lock (pg_advisory_lock, not pg_advisory_xact_lock — intentionally, per the ISS-0131/GH-424 comment at line 104-116, because the per-migration transactions inside runForSchema would release an xact_lock prematurely) on a connection borrowed from the pool, and releases it via `defer releaseAdvisoryLock(lock_conn, tenant_id_str) catch {}` (line 124) before the connection is returned to the pool via the outer `defer pool.release(lock_conn)` (line 122). Because pg_advisory_lock is SESSION-scoped (tied to the physical Postgres backend, not the logical Conn wrapper), any path that returns the connection to Pool.release() without releaseAdvisoryLock having actually executed leaves the physical backend still holding the lock from Postgres's point of view — and since the connection is now back in the pool's idle set, whichever future caller acquires that same physical connection will find it already lock-holding (from a completed, unrelated logical operation), explaining the observed `idle` state with the lock still granted. Candidate mechanisms: (1) releaseAdvisoryLock's own `conn.exec(...) catch return ProvisionError.QueryFailed` (line 71) can itself fail without raising past the `catch {}` at the call site (line 124), silently swallowing a release failure; (2) any early-return/panic inside the block between acquireAdvisoryLock succeeding and its defer running would skip the release (though Zig defers should cover ordinary early returns — worth confirming no exhaustive @panic path bypasses this); (3) Pool.release() (src/db/pool.zig:834+) does not itself verify or force-clear any advisory lock state before returning a connection to the idle set, so it has no defense-in-depth against a caller's release()-order-of-operations bug. Not yet isolated to one of these three with certainty — needs a BACKEND-DEV investigation with reproduction under a debugger or added logging around the release path.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause is isolated to a specific code path (one of the three candidates above, or another)
releaseAdvisoryLock's failure path no longer silently swallows an error that would leave the lock held (either surface it, retry, or add a pool-level safety net)
A full zig build test run (or an equivalent targeted concurrent-provisioning stress test) completes without hanging, run at least 10 times consecutively with no recurrence

Consider whether Pool.release() should defensively call pg_advisory_unlock_all() on the connection before returning it to the idle set, as defense-in-depth against any future caller that fails to release a session-scoped lock it acquired
evidence_file: tests/reports/report-2026-08-07-WF03-GH528-20260807.yaml — 'full_suite_test_result' section documents both hangs with pg_stat_activity/pg_locks output captured live during the incident
notes: Discovered incidentally while verifying an unrelated fix (GH #528 / ISS-0207, a test-file-only change to tests/unit/service_task_test.zig with zero relation to src/db/provisioning.zig). Forwarded per the CLAUDE.md scope boundary rather than fixed in that run — GH-528's own acceptance criteria were independently verified via a scoped build step (zig build test-bpm-src) that does not exercise the full-suite concurrency this defect requires to manifest, so GH-528 was not blocked by this discovery. This defect is a genuine severity concern in its own right: it can hang ANY full-suite zig build test invocation, in any workspace, for any unrelated change, once the right interleaving occurs — worth prioritizing given how disruptive an indefinite hang is compared to a normal test failure.
final_resolution: provisionTenantSchema() (src/db/provisioning.zig) restructured to acquire one connection and hold it, together with the tenant advisory lock, across every step of the actual provisioning work (idempotency check, bpm_provision_tenant_schema() call, timestamp update, tenant promotion), releasing both together on every exit path -- fixing the confirmed root cause (lock scope closed before the work it claimed to serialize). runForSchema() (the migration step) deliberately keeps its own separate connection; its signature takes no *Conn parameter, so it structurally cannot share the tenant lock's connection -- CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR independently re-derived this from source and confirmed no cross-lock deadlock exists (disjoint connections, disjoint lock keyspace vs. the global migration lock). Pool.release() (src/db/pool.zig) now calls pg_advisory_unlock_all() on every connection before it re-enters the idle pool, as defense-in-depth. tests/unit/test_api08_auth.zig's ensureTenantDefaultSchema() (added by ISS-0209) had grown its own redundant outer lock on the same key that only worked because the original bug made the real lock a no-op; removed now that the real lock is correct, with the ISS-0209 destructive DROP SCHEMA CASCADE fallback re-confirmed absent. Verified: 12-thread same-tenant stress test (tests/integration/iss0129_migration_run_advisory_lock_test.zig) went from stalling at 24/96 calls (180s cap) to completing 96/96 in 2.2-3.3s, confirmed across 4 independent runs by two different agents (BACKEND-DEV x2, TEST-RUNNER x2). zig build test: 939/1003 pass, 64 skip, 0 fail, matching the pre-fix baseline exactly across all 4 runs. Zero stray advisory locks or non-idle backends confirmed after every run.
confirmed_root_cause: The comment at src/db/provisioning.zig:104-105 claims the block at lines 117-125 'serialize[s] the whole provisionTenantSchema pass under a session-level advisory lock', but the code does NOT do this. The advisory lock is acquired (line 123) AND released (line 124's defer) inside its own nested `{ }` block that closes at line 125 -- fully before Step 2 (idempotency check, line 128) even begins. So the lock provides mutual exclusion over nothing except its own acquire+immediately-release micro-section; it does not cover Steps 2 through 6a (idempotency check, bpm_provision_tenant_schema() call, migrations.Migrations.runForSchema(), tenant_schemas timestamp update, public.tenant promotion) at all. Multiple concurrent provisionTenantSchema() calls for the SAME tenant_id therefore race freely through the unprotected Steps 2-6a -- exactly the C40P01/race class the comment states this lock exists to prevent (ISS-0131/GH-424). Under that unprotected concurrency, every racing call's Step 5 (src/db/migrations.zig runForSchema(), provisioning.zig:182) contends for a SEPARATE global (not per-tenant) advisory-lock keyspace -- MIGRATIONS_LOCK_KEY_SQL = pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('bpm.migrations.runForSchema')) at migrations.zig:31-32/463 -- which is transaction-scoped and held on the pool connection for the duration of each per-migration transaction (BEGIN..COMMIT, migrations.zig:422-538) while that connection is checked out of the pool (not released). Additionally, provisioning.zig Step 4's SQL call to public.bpm_provision_tenant_schema() (line 176) itself takes a THIRD, per-schema-keyed pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(v_schema_name)) inside its own implicit transaction (migrations/060_schema_per_tenant_bootstrap.sql:89). None of these three lock layers actually serializes the higher-level provisionTenantSchema() pass they were each individually designed to protect a piece of, because the outer 'pass-level' lock in provisioning.zig closes before the pass's real work starts. Empirically reproduced: a targeted stress test (12 threads calling provisionTenantSchema for the SAME tenant_id x 8 rounds each, shared Pool with pool_size=3, matching the connection-scarcity + high-contention conditions of a full-suite zig build test run) completed only 24/96 calls before stalling completely for the remainder of a 180s hard-cap wait, then returned PoolExhausted on 8 of 12 worker threads when force-terminated -- i.e. 3-of-3 pool connections were checked out and never returned to idle_count during the stall, with pg_stat_activity/pg_locks on the test database showing ZERO advisory locks held and ZERO active queries at the time of the stall (only idle Client/ClientRead backends). This is consistent with connections becoming stuck checked-out (not server-side lock-blocked at the moment sampled) somewhere in the racing Steps 2-6a / runForSchema/bpm_provision_tenant_schema chain once the outer lock's false serialization guarantee is exposed under heavy same-tenant concurrency. The originally-investigated candidate (conn._is_valid flipping false between acquireAdvisoryLock succeeding and releaseAdvisoryLock running, provisioning.zig:123-124) was traced through pool.zig's Conn.exec (pool.zig:467-488) and ruled out: exec() has no code path that both sets _is_valid=false AND returns success, and nothing else touches lock_conn between lines 123 and 124, so that pairing cannot desync within a single provisionTenantSchema call. The real defect is structural/architectural (a lock scope that does not cover the section its own comment says it covers), not a transient connection-validity race.
reproduction_method: Code-path analysis (traced provisioning.zig lines 117-125 against Step 2-6a below it; confirmed via direct source read that the advisory-lock block's own nested scope closes at line 125, before Step 2 begins) combined with a live empirical stress reproduction: temporarily appended a test to tests/integration/iss0129_migration_run_advisory_lock_test.zig (12 threads x 8 rounds, same tenant_id, shared Pool pool_size=3, run via `zig build test-integration-iss0129` against BPM_TEST_DB_URL=postgres://bpm:bpm@localhost:5453/bpm_test in workspace r-co-2) with a progress-watchdog polling pg_stat_activity/pg_locks. Result: progress stalled at 24/96 for the remainder of a 180s hard-cap, workers force-terminated with error.PoolExhausted (8 of 12), confirming pool connections were leaked/stuck-checked-out under same-tenant concurrent provisioning load -- the exact condition (many test binaries provisioning tenant_default concurrently) that produces the original full-suite hang. The temporary repro test was reverted (git checkout) after evidence was captured; it is not part of the permanent test suite. All spawned test.exe/zig.exe processes exited on their own after the run; verified via `tasklist` and confirmed zero non-idle backends and zero held advisory locks remained on bpm_test via pg_stat_activity/pg_locks before completing this diagnosis.

root_cause_precision.primary_defect: src/db/provisioning.zig:117-125 — the session-scoped advisory-lock block closes (releases the lock and returns lock_conn to the pool) BEFORE Steps 2-6a (lines 127-259) execute, so the lock does not serialize provisionTenantSchema() as its own comment (lines 104-105) claims.
contributing_factors: src/db/migrations.zig:31-32,463 — MIGRATIONS_LOCK_KEY_SQL is a single GLOBAL key (not per-tenant/per-schema), so it serializes ALL concurrent migration work across every tenant onto one transaction at a time, holding each contending connection checked out of the pool for the duration of its wait.

migrations/060_schema_per_tenant_bootstrap.sql:89 — bpm_provision_tenant_schema() takes its own per-schema pg_advisory_xact_lock independently of the Zig-side locks, a third uncoordinated lock layer in the same call chain.
